plumbing.review:
Two findings need fixes:

- **[P2] Outside files can pass containment.** [shell.go:46](shell.go:46) reuses `inside()` after resolving symlinks. That helper strips `/private/`, so distinct directories such as `work` and `work` become equivalent. An escaping symlink can therefore publish its outside target as a workspace file. Compare canonical paths directly with `filepath.Rel` and `filepath.IsLocal`, and add regression coverage.

- **[P2] Symlink directory changes can report the wrong file.** [shell.go:242](shell.go:242) resolves `cd` physically. With `link -> real/sub`, `cd link/.. && cat top.go` reads the workspace’s `top.go` under default logical shell semantics, but the classifier records `real/top.go`. Preserve logical `cd` semantics or classify ambiguous forms as `other`, with regression coverage.

The acceptance sources match the ratified plan exactly, and the factory reports passing checks. They miss these cases. I found no weakened tests, command execution, network calls, unrelated scope changes, or material style problems. I did not rerun tests under the read-only constraint. The decision refinement remains the merger’s responsibility.

VERDICT: changes needed — fix canonical containment and symlink-aware directory handling, and add regression tests.
